title: Setup checks
intro: Setup checks reviews the services and settings this installation needs. Use it after installation or configuration changes, then follow the advice beside each warning or failure.
You need View settings. Changing a linked setting may need another permission. These checks use the same list as openldr doctor. Read Start here for command-line setup.
Use your own installation results. The pictures show an isolated development installation with deliberate missing configuration. No sample data is required.

tasks.title: Read the current readiness report
intro: Use this before treating an installation as ready for staff. The checks run when the page opens.
steps: Open your user menu at the bottom left, choose Settings, then select Setup checks.
Read the number of failed checks and warnings. If neither exists, the summary says All checks passed.
Read the service detail and suggested next action. This test installation reports a blob-storage service failure. Follow the advice for your own result.
A warning needs review even when the service is available. The example warns that Laboratory name still uses the shipped default.
Skipped means the check did not apply. It does not mean that an unused feature has been configured.
tasks.result: You know which checks need attention and which advice applies to this installation.

tasks.title: Follow a warning and check the correction
intro: Use a linked setting page to correct a problem. This example corrects a laboratory name and missing time zone on PostgreSQL.
steps: Select Open Laboratory beside the Laboratory name warning.
Enter your actual issuing laboratory name. The picture uses Documentation laboratory in a test installation.
Set the time zone when applicable
For PostgreSQL or MySQL, enter your named local time zone. The example uses Africa/Dar_es_Salaam. On SQL Server, follow the page advice and supply the Windows zone in each report run instead.
Open the Laboratory page dots and select Save.
Select Setup checks in Settings. Opening it runs the checks again.
tasks.result: The corrected Laboratory name and Time zone checks show Passed. Other warnings or failures still need attention.

tasks.title: Run the checks again
intro: Use this after configuration changes or after a service recovers.
steps: Select the dots at the top right of Setup checks.
Select Run again. Wait for the checks to finish.
tasks.result: The new summary shows the current result. Read the remaining failed checks and warnings.

tasks.title: Read setup checks on a phone
intro: Use the same page on a phone. Each check includes its status and advice.
steps: Open Setup checks and read the summary at the top.
Read each check detail and any link or next action.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: No practice records are required. In a test installation, correct a genuine laboratory-name or time-zone warning, save it, then run the checks again. Do not introduce a service failure for this exercise.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: The report describes the checks at the time they ran. All checks passed does not prove every report, feed or staff workflow. Some repairs need server configuration outside Studio.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The checks could not run. Check the API connection and server log, then try Run again.
Services failed. Follow the displayed health-command advice and inspect the named service.
Sign-in warns that it is switched off. Turn off the development authentication bypass in server configuration before real use.
A linked page is unavailable. Ask an administrator with permission to edit that setting.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Laboratory for issuing-lab details. Read Connectors for connection tests. Read Start here for installation and command-line setup.
